title: Fast ‘Frame Based’ Precession Mapping Technique for Multimodal STEM Applications
content: The field of mapping applications in STEM reaches from spectroscopy with EDS and EELS, metrology with strain/orientation mapping to E/B field measurements using 4D STEM techniques. All these experiments benefit from not using a scan with a beam with fixed tilt, but by acquiring the signals under dynamic beam tilt conditions. Normally Precession is executed by rotating the beam in each scan position with a fixed tilt before visiting the next scan point [1]. This approach has the disadvantage that due to lens aberrations the beam shape degrades and the imperfections of the scan/descan coil synchronization the angular resolution is compromised. There is no method available to correct for this after the experiments.
